info.senderName: Nimbus Resilience Solutions on behalf of Sample County Emergency Management
info.headline: LEAVE NOW to escape a DANGEROUS WILDFIRE approaching Cleveland County, OK
info.description: At 4:19 PM, a dangerous wildfire was burning in northwestern Cleveland County, approximately 6 miles northwest of Norman, spreading quickly east. Wildfires can damage or destroy homes and other structures, and can injure or kill people and animals.
info.instruction: LEAVE NOW from Cleveland County, OK to avoid risk of injury or death from this wildfire. Roads may be blocked by smoke or fire. Never drive into heavy smoke.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 24 at 3:15PM MDT until August 24 at 6:15PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
info.description: FFWGJTThe National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a * Flash Flood Warning for... The Lee and P-L Gulch burn scars in... Central Rio Blanco County in northwestern Colorado... * Until 615 PM MDT. * At 315 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain over the Lee and P-L Gulch Burn Scars. Between 0.1 and 0.3 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 3 inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scars will result in debris flow. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials. HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing flash flooding in and around the Lee and P-L Gulch Burn Scars. SOURCE...Radar indicated. IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the Lee and P-L Gulch Burn Scars. * Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Mainly rural areas of Central Rio Blanco County.
info.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches in the Lee and P-L Gulch Burn Scars. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.
Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of creeks, roads and normally dry arroyos is likely. The heavy rains will likely trigger rockslides, mudslides and debris flows in steep terrain, especially in and around these areas.
Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law enforcement and request they pass this information to the National Weather Service when you can do so safely.

parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 6:15 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.

National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 6:15 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.
